text:
Maria: Quick RFC follow-up — proposing a lightweight mTLS "shim" we can deploy in customer VPCs (or their transit) to act as a fallback when Private Endpoint/Privatelink paths degrade. Goal: keep control plane reachable without forcing customers to open broad egress or require EIPs.

Jonathan: By "shim" do you mean a tunnel or a TCP proxy? preserving source IP is the main ask from infra teams.

Maria: Tunnel-ish. Something that terminates mTLS to our CP and forwards connections to local agents, ideally preserving src IP so logs/rls still map to tenant. Prefer not to SNAT per-tenant.

Sara: WireGuard preserves src IP but needs key mgmt + kernel module. TLS-over-TCP proxy is simpler but usually SNATs.

Alex: Can we use a regional relay pool we control and an ephemeral mapping table so we avoid per-tenant EIP? e.g., relay <-> cp with ephemeral 1:1 mappings for sessions. Means more operator state.

Maria: Thinking of hybrid: a lightweight mTLS shim that speaks our CP protocol upstream and uses an encapsulation locally (ipip/wireguard) to preserve src. The shim would be customer-owned (small binary) or operator-run in managed transit.

Jonathan: Main tradeoffs:
- WireGuard: +preserves src, low latency; - key distribution + noisy to onboard customers.
- TLS tunnel: +easy key rot + leverages our existing cert infra; - likely requires SNAT or socket proxying.

infra-bot: perf-test summary uploaded: https://ci/internal/relays/wireguard-spike -> p50: +4ms, p95: +12ms (compared to current privatelink baseline).

Sara: Obs/trace requirements: shim must inject trace headers, emit health checks to CP, and expose a local metrics endpoint for customers to scrape (or we can pull). Also important: detect and fail-open semantics so app traffic doesn't blackhole.

Alex: Network restrictions in some regulated tenants: GRE/ipip might be blocked. We need an option that falls back to TCP-multiplexing. Maybe shim negotiation: try udp/wg, fallback to tls-tcp.

Maria: Agreed. Also key management options:
- Option A: customer-provisioned keys (minimal trust, more ops on their side)
- Option B: CP-issued ephemeral certs via onboarding token (more UX work but smoother).

Jonathan: Security checks: mutual auth + short-lived certs, attestation that shim binary hasn't been tampered (sig verification). Need to add to compliance checklist for Private offering.

Sara: Ops concerns: if we preserve src IP we must ensure SNAT doesn't happen in intermediate NAT gateways. Recommend an e2e test matrix: per-region NAT topology + shim mode.

Maria: Implementation spike plan:
- Spike A: wireguard-based shim (preserve src) — owners @Maria + @Alex — 2w
- Spike B: tls-tcp shim (fallback path) — owner @Sara — 1w
- Add CI tests for src-IP fidelity and A/B latency comparisons.

Alex: Rollout plan: staged canary to 5 pilot customers. Add automatic fallback in agent: if privatelink times out 3x, switch to shim route with exponential backoff.

Jonathan: Rollback: if shim causes route flaps we pin customers back to managed privatelink and disable shim via remote flag. Also alerting: high ERROR rate on shim -> auto-disable to avoid cascades.

infra-bot: checklist created: https://tickets/internal/RELAYS-2345 — includes QA steps, cost estimate, and security review slot.

Maria: Perf + cost note — wireguard increases egress on our relays but reduces gateway SNAT cost. Need cost model spike.

Sara: Small config sketch for shim to discuss during spike:

```yaml
listen: 0.0.0.0:8443
mode: mtls-shim
upstream: cp.redwood.internal:443
encapsulation: wireguard # or tls-tcp
preserve_src: true
advertise_routes: ["10.200.0.0/16"]
health_check: /healthz
```

Alex: +1 to adding a "debug-state" endpoint so SREs can inspect ephemeral mappings without exposing keys. Must auth with short-lived token.

Maria: Action items:
- @Maria/@Alex: run wireguard spike (2w) and report latency/cost + onboarding checklist.
- @Sara: spike tls-tcp fallback + obs contract (1w).
- @Jonathan: draft compliance bullet points and rollback playbook.
- Schedule sync next Tue to pick candidate approach.

Jonathan: Sounds good. One more question: how does this interact with Dedicated instances (reserved capacity)? We need to ensure shim doesn't route to shared hosted CP if customer is on dedicated control plane.

Maria: Good call — keep routing orthogonal: shim should be able to talk to either hosted CP or customer's dedicated CP endpoint, configurable at install time. We'll add a routing param.

Sara: :thumbsup:

Alex: I'll stub the repo + README this afternoon -> link in thread when ready.

Maria: thanks all — posting spike ticket and adding to architecture backlog.
